title: Tenant boundary metadata + switchover safeguards for private/VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Private / VPC customers require cryptographically auditable proof that (1) their data stayed inside declared boundaries, (2) retention policies were applied, and (3) any regional switchover followed constrained guardrails. Current residency attestations are manual, lack tenant-scoped metadata, and do not tie to the exact switchover choreography used by the orchestration layer. This ticket scopes an engineering plan to: 1) add tenant-bound residency metadata to node claims and storage snapshots; 2) implement a switchover constraint enforcer that validates regional failover policies (no forced evacuation to disallowed regions, rate-limited evacuation); 3) produce tamper-evident evidence bundles and an automated reporting pipeline for compliance exports.
acceptance_criteria: Node claim and snapshot objects include immutable tenant-scoped residency metadata (region, VPC IDs, retention TTL, crypto-hash of snapshot)
Switchover enforcer denies or queues evacuation requests that violate tenant policy and emits explainable events to the audit log
Evidence bundles (signed JSONL) are produced after any switchover or retention purge including timelines, responsible actor, and verification hashes
Automated export task uploads evidence bundles to customer S3/GCS endpoints or retention vaults on demand
E2E integration tests that simulate a constrained failover (primary->secondary) and assert policy enforcement + evidence bundle validity
implementation_notes: Plan: (a) extend node-claim proto to include tenant_id, declared_regions, retention_tier, and a signing_key_id; (b) add a small validator service (residency-enforcer) that subscribes to orchestration intentions and approves/blocks switchover; (c) hook bundle-generator into the orchestration state machine so a signed bundle is emitted at start/end of switchover and after scheduled retention purges. Cryptography: use KMS-backed ECDSA key per-customer (rotateable) and include verification metadata in exports. Storage: evidence bundles written to tenant-specific evidence-store with immutable retention TTL. Telemetry: expose metrics for blocked evacuations, crypto-sign failures, and bundle generation latency.
tradeoffs: Adding per-tenant keys increases KMS traffic and operational complexity but gives stronger non-repudiation vs. a shared platform key
Blocking evacuations synchronously could increase failover latency; chosen approach is to attempt synchronous validation then fall back to a queued, operator-notified evacuation window (configurable)
Including full snapshot hashes in each bundle increases size; we include only root object hashes and provide artifact pointers to signed snapshot manifests to reduce bundle size
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete. Validated KMS per-tenant keypair creation and signing with staged test tenant. Proof-of-concept bundle format (JSONL) prototyped.
2026-03-04: Residency metadata added to node-claim proto in feature branch: feat/residency-metadata. Unit tests added for serialization and immutability checks.

2026-03-07: Residency-enforcer prototype subscribed to orchestration intentions and correctly blocked an intentional test evacuation from eu-west to us-east for tenant with EU-only policy. Logged events include policy id and blocking reason.

2026-03-09: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4216 (includes enforcer integration and bundle emitter hook). Requesting design review from Linnea Chen and security review from Devon Patel.

2026-03-10: Integration test failing intermittently when KMS throttles; added retry-with-backoff and metric to alert SRE on retries > 5 within 5m. Filing follow-up to capacity-plan KMS usage (ENG-92510).
